q1_issues.issue: The fused compound genetically_modified_food emits only its head genus; 'genetically modified' is an adjectival property predicable of the referent ('the food is genetically modified'), and the modifier-genus rule is stated as determined, not optional, so the modifier link appears to be missing.
'other' in 'other technologies' is dropped with no record, so the contrastive restriction on the second Through argument is lost.
The state witness is named sk_focus_1 while its class is 'focused', breaking the sk_<class>_<n> minting convention and inviting collision with a genuine focus event.

q2_gaps: 'other N' as a modifier — no licensed encoding for the exclusion/contrast it marks

a gerund clause as the object of an adjective's PP complement ('focused on eliminating world hunger') — the instruction set covers a noun's argument PP ('a vehicle for V-ing') and control/causative complements, but not an adjective's PP taking a clausal argument
an adverb+participle modifier inside a fused compound ('genetically modified') — decomposing once to single-word lemmas cannot express a two-word modifier
adjectival-passive vs eventive-passive routing for 'is focused on' — the participle-as-modifier test is stated for prenominal modifiers, not for a copular 'is V-ed on' predicate
notes: The strongest part of the batch: the 'sponsored by' reduced relative with the by-phrase as Agent, the multi-word department name as one symbol + Name + separate kind atom, the adjective-PP-complement reification with the flat copular dual-emit, and the tenseless top-level complement event all follow the instruction set. Only the compound-modifier genus and the dropped 'other' are at issue.
